In-scope systems.value: Every asset in the CMDB scanned by Qualys/Tenable, plus cloud posture findings and penetration-test scope, consolidated in the GRC platform risk register

Compliance procedure documented.value: Enterprise Cybersecurity Risk Assessment Procedure — asset scoping, vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, control-gap rating, and severity-based remediation SLAs

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Info Security Officer and ratified by the Board Risk Committee; reviewed annually or after a material incident

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual assessment closes and reports to the Board Risk Committee ahead of the FCA Handbook SUP 16 annual return cycle; Critical findings remediated within 30 days, High within 90 days

checklist.step: Scope the annual assessment and freeze the asset inventory
actions: Pull the current asset inventory from the CMDB (Configuration Items ▸ Server/App/Cloud Resource) and export the in-scope list to the GRC platform risk register.
Cross-reference the Operational Resilience Lead's important-business-services map (SYSC 15A) to flag which assets support an important business service.
Confirm scope with the Chief Risk Officer and record sign-off in the assessment charter.
Freeze the scope list and timestamp it as the assessment baseline.
checklist.done: the asset inventory is pulled, cross-referenced to important business services, and frozen as the assessment baseline.

checklist.step: Run authenticated vulnerability scans across the estate
actions: In Qualys/Tenable open Scans ▸ New Scan, select the frozen asset group, and apply the authenticated-credential scan template.
Launch the scan against on-prem, IaaS and PaaS assets and monitor for scan failures or unreachable hosts.
Export results (CSV/XML) with CVSS base score, affected asset and patch reference for every finding.
Re-queue any host that failed authentication and log the reason (credential rotation, firewall block).
checklist.done: a completed authenticated scan export exists for every in-scope asset, with failures re-queued or logged.

checklist.step: Commission and scope the annual penetration test
actions: Select the external penetration testing vendor and issue a statement of work covering the internet-facing perimeter, the customer portal, and one critical internal segment.
Agree rules of engagement (test window, excluded systems, escalation contact) with the Penetration Tester and vendor lead.
Notify IT Operations and the SOC of the test window so alerts are not misclassified as real attacks.
checklist.done: a signed statement of work and rules of engagement exist and the SOC has been notified of the test window.

checklist.step: Execute the penetration test and document exploitable findings
actions: Run reconnaissance, exploitation and post-exploitation against the agreed scope within the approved window.
Record each finding with CVSS score, affected asset, proof-of-concept evidence and business impact.
Deliver the draft report to the Chief Info Security Officer within 5 business days of test completion.
checklist.done: a penetration test report with CVSS-scored, evidenced findings is delivered within 5 business days of test completion.

checklist.step: Review cloud security posture findings
actions: Open the cloud provider's security center (Azure Defender for Cloud / AWS Security Hub) and export the current secure-score findings for every subscription/account in scope.
Cross-check each High/Critical finding against the CMDB to confirm asset ownership.
Add cloud findings to the consolidated risk register alongside the vulnerability scan and pen-test results.
checklist.done: cloud security posture findings are exported, owner-matched, and merged into the consolidated register.

checklist.step: Consolidate and rate every finding in the GRC platform
actions: Import the vulnerability scan export, pen-test findings and cloud posture findings into the GRC platform's Risk Register module.
Assign each finding a severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low) using the CVSS score plus exploitability and business-impact modifiers.
De-duplicate findings that reference the same root cause across multiple assets.
Assign each finding a remediation SLA: Critical 30 days, High 90 days, Medium 180 days, Low next assessment cycle.
checklist.done: every finding is de-duplicated, severity-rated and carries an SLA in the GRC risk register.

checklist.step: Assign remediation owners and open tickets
actions: For each open finding, identify the asset/application owner from the CMDB and assign the remediation ticket to them.
Set the ticket due date to the SLA date computed in the risk register and link the ticket back to the risk register entry.
Escalate any finding without an identifiable owner to the Chief Technology Officer within 3 business days.
checklist.done: every finding has an owned, SLA-dated remediation ticket linked to its risk register entry.

checklist.step: Track remediation progress against SLA
actions: Run a weekly report of open remediation tickets filtered by SLA due date within 14 days.
Follow up with ticket owners approaching or past SLA and log their status update on the ticket.
Escalate tickets more than 5 business days past SLA to the Chief Info Security Officer for exception handling.
checklist.done: a weekly SLA report exists and every past-due ticket has a logged follow-up or escalation.

checklist.step: Validate fixes with a targeted re-scan
actions: For each ticket marked resolved, run a targeted re-scan of the specific asset and CVE/plugin ID in Qualys/Tenable.
Confirm the finding no longer appears in the re-scan result before closing the ticket.
Where the finding persists, reopen the ticket and reset the SLA clock from the reopen date.
checklist.done: every 'resolved' finding is confirmed clear by a targeted re-scan before its ticket is closed.

checklist.step: Update the operational resilience impact tolerance mapping
actions: Review any Critical or High finding tied to an important business service and assess whether it affects the service's impact tolerance under SYSC 15A.
Update the important-business-service risk map with the residual risk rating until remediation completes.
Notify the Chief Risk Officer of any service whose impact tolerance is now at risk of breach.
checklist.done: the important-business-service risk map reflects every open Critical/High finding and the CRO is notified of any tolerance risk.

checklist.step: Draft the annual assessment report and residual risk statement
actions: Summarize scope, methodology, findings by severity, remediation status and residual risk into the annual report template.
State the residual risk position against the Board-approved risk appetite.
Circulate the draft to the Chief Risk Officer for review before the Board Risk Committee submission deadline.
checklist.done: a draft report with a stated residual risk position is circulated to the CRO ahead of the committee deadline.

checklist.step: Present findings to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Upload the final assessment report and executive summary to the board portal ahead of the scheduled Risk Committee meeting.
Present the residual risk position, top findings and remediation roadmap at the meeting.
Capture committee questions, directives and the meeting minute reference against the assessment record.
checklist.done: the report is uploaded to the board portal, presented, and committee minutes are captured against the assessment record.

checklist.step: Update controls and policy based on systemic findings
actions: Identify any finding pattern indicating a control gap (missing patch cadence, weak segmentation) rather than a one-off asset issue.
Draft the control or policy change and route it through the standard policy approval workflow.
Communicate the updated control requirement to IT Operations and application owners.
checklist.done: every systemic finding pattern has a corresponding control or policy update routed for approval.

checklist.step: Log exceptions for overdue or accepted-risk findings
actions: For any finding past SLA with no remediation plan, log a formal risk exception with root cause and a revised target date.
Route risk-acceptance requests to the Chief Info Security Officer and, for Critical findings, the Chief Risk Officer for approval.
Record the approved exception's expiry date and required compensating control.
checklist.done: every overdue or accepted finding has a logged, approved exception with an expiry date and compensating control.

checklist.step: Retain assessment evidence in the compliance repository
actions: Upload the scan exports, pen-test report, risk register extract, remediation tickets and committee minutes to the compliance evidence repository under the assessment year folder.
Apply the 6-year retention label required under FCA Handbook SYSC 9.
Confirm the folder is indexed and retrievable by asset, finding severity and remediation status.
checklist.done: the full assessment evidence set is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by asset and severity.

testing.step: Build the population of findings and remediation tickets for the period
actions: Export every finding opened in the assessment period from the GRC platform risk register, with severity, owner, SLA date and status.
Reconcile the finding count to the vulnerability scan export and the penetration test report to confirm nothing was dropped during import.
Resolve any count mismatch with the Security GRC Analyst before sampling.
testing.done: the finding population reconciles to the source scan and pen-test exports.

testing.step: Verify scan and pen-test coverage against the frozen asset inventory
actions: Compare the assets actually scanned/tested to the frozen scope list from the assessment charter.
List any in-scope asset with no scan result or pen-test coverage as a coverage gap.
Confirm coverage gaps were logged as exceptions rather than silently dropped.
testing.done: every in-scope asset is accounted for by a scan result, a pen-test result, or a logged coverage-gap exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample of findings
actions: Take 100% of Critical findings and any finding tied to an important business service.
Take 20 additional findings at random (seeded, reproducible) across High/Medium severities.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all Critical/important-business-service findings.

testing.step: Re-perform severity rating on the sample
actions: Independently re-derive the CVSS score and severity rating for each sampled finding from the original scan/pen-test evidence, without viewing the recorded rating first.
Compare the independently derived rating to the recorded rating and log any mismatch.
Note any case where a lower severity appears to have been assigned to avoid the tighter SLA.
testing.done: each sampled finding has an independent severity re-derivation compared to the recorded rating, with mismatches logged.

testing.step: Re-scan the sample to confirm current remediation status
actions: For each sampled finding marked resolved, run an independent targeted re-scan of the specific asset and CVE/plugin ID.
Confirm the finding does not reappear; where it does, flag as a false-closure exception.
Capture the re-scan output into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled resolved finding is independently re-scanned and confirmed clear, or flagged as a false closure.

testing.step: Trace SLA dates and closure timing
actions: For each sampled finding, recompute the SLA due date from severity and the finding-open date per the documented SLA table.
Compare the recomputed SLA date to the ticket's actual close date.
Flag any finding closed after its SLA date with no approved exception on file.
testing.done: every sampled finding's SLA maths is recomputed and any late closure without an approved exception is flagged.

testing.step: Test that overdue findings have an approved, expiring exception
actions: Pull every finding past SLA in the sample and confirm a risk exception exists in the GRC platform.
Verify the exception carries the required approver (CISO, or CRO for Critical) signature and an expiry date.
Flag any overdue finding lacking an approved exception as a control failure, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled overdue finding is backed by an approver-signed, expiry-dated exception or is flagged as a failure.

testing.step: Confirm Board Risk Committee reporting occurred
actions: Open the board portal and confirm the assessment report and executive summary were uploaded ahead of the scheduled Risk Committee meeting.
Cross-check the committee minutes reference captured in the assessment record against the actual minute text.
Confirm any committee directive was tracked to closure.
testing.done: the board portal upload, minute reference and any committee directive are all verified against the record.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each test exception found above, describing the gap and its compliance impact.
Assign a root cause category and an owner for remediation.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into the next assessment cycle as mandatory retest items.
testing.done: every test exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the population and compare to the zero-tolerance threshold for Critical findings and the 90%-on-time threshold for High/Medium.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence gathered.
Have an independent reviewer who authored none of the sampled re-performance work sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any open exceptions to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is reported to the Board Risk Committee and filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns continuous operation of MFA, encryption and access-review controls across all in-scope systems

Citation verified against current regula.value: FCA Handbook SYSC 3.2.6R (systems and controls) and SYSC 6.1.1R (financial crime systems and controls), cross-referenced with UK GDPR Article 32 (security of processing), re-read at control-design date (rep: United Kingdom)

In-scope processes.value: Identity and access management (provisioning, MFA enrolment, periodic access recertification) and data-at-rest/in-transit encryption across policy admin, claims and customer-data systems

In-scope systems.value: MFA enforcement policies, conditional access rules and quarterly access-review campaigns run from the IAM platform; privileged accounts vaulted in the PAM tool

Compliance procedure documented.value: Access Control & Encryption Standard — MFA enrolment, privileged access via PAM, quarterly access recertification, encryption key management and rotation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Info Security Officer and IT Security Manager; reviewed annually or on a material control failure

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Controls operate continuously; each quarterly access-review campaign must close within 30 days of launch and MFA coverage is verified monthly

Deadline reminders configured.value: IAM platform campaign reminders at day 15/25/30 of each quarterly access-review cycle; monthly MFA-coverage report auto-generated to the IT Security Manager

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: MFA enrolment logs, access-review campaign results and encryption key rotation logs retained 6 years per FCA Handbook SYSC 9

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any account found without required MFA, an unattested access grant, or unencrypted transmission is logged as an exception with root cause

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Each remediated exception is signed off with evidence of the corrective configuration change

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All privileged and standard user accounts on in-scope systems as of the test date, plus every quarterly access-review campaign completed in the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% MFA coverage required on privileged and customer-data-facing accounts; ≥98% access-review campaign completion within the 30-day window to pass

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; the test runs quarterly, aligned to each access-review campaign close

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not administer the IAM platform or hold access-provisioning rights

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly access-control test workpaper (account population, sample, IAM platform screenshots, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: MFA coverage report, access-review campaign completion report and encryption key rotation log, presentable within 5 business days of a supervisory request

Regulator response path.value: IT Security Manager owns the technical response; Chief Info Security Officer clears any submission before it is sent

checklist.step: Define the control baseline and system scope
actions: Export the in-scope application and system list from the CMDB, tiered by data sensitivity (customer PII, policy/claims data, internal).
For each tier, record the required controls: MFA method, encryption standard (AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit) and access-review frequency.
Circulate the baseline to application owners for acknowledgement and file the signed baseline in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: every in-scope system has a documented, owner-acknowledged control baseline by data-sensitivity tier.

checklist.step: Configure MFA enforcement policies
actions: In Okta/Azure AD open Security ▸ Multifactor Authentication and set the required factor (authenticator app or hardware key) per application group.
Apply a conditional-access/app sign-on policy requiring MFA for every login to customer-data-facing and privileged applications.
Test the policy against a pilot account group and confirm enforcement before rolling out tenant-wide.
Publish the rollout date to application owners.
checklist.done: an MFA enforcement policy is configured, pilot-tested and rolled out for every in-scope application group.

checklist.step: Enrol privileged accounts in the PAM vault
actions: In CyberArk open Accounts ▸ Add Account for each privileged/administrative credential and onboard it into the safe.
Enable automatic password rotation and session recording for every onboarded account.
Remove any standing local administrator credential once the PAM-managed equivalent is verified working.
checklist.done: every privileged account is onboarded to the PAM vault with rotation and session recording enabled.

checklist.step: Verify encryption at rest and in transit
actions: For each in-scope database and storage account, confirm encryption-at-rest is enabled (native TDE or platform-managed encryption) and record the key management method.
Run a TLS configuration scan against each public and internal endpoint and confirm TLS 1.2 or higher with no deprecated cipher suites.
Log any system found without the required encryption as a control gap and open a remediation ticket.
checklist.done: encryption-at-rest and TLS configuration is verified for every in-scope system, with gaps ticketed.

checklist.step: Run the monthly MFA coverage report
actions: In the IAM platform open Reports ▸ MFA Enrollment and export the coverage report by application group.
Identify accounts without an enrolled MFA factor, especially privileged and customer-data-facing accounts.
Send the exception list to account owners requiring enrolment within 5 business days.
checklist.done: a monthly MFA coverage report is produced and every unenrolled account has an owner notification on file.

checklist.step: Launch the quarterly access recertification campaign
actions: In the IAM platform open Certifications ▸ New Campaign, scope it to all in-scope applications, and assign each user's direct manager as reviewer.
Set the campaign due date to 30 days from launch and enable automated reminder emails.
Publish the campaign kickoff notice to reviewers with instructions on approve/revoke actions.
checklist.done: a scoped, manager-assigned access recertification campaign is launched with a 30-day due date and reminders enabled.

checklist.step: Reviewers complete access recertification
actions: Open the assigned certification campaign in the IAM platform and review each direct report's entitlement list.
Attest 'approve' for access still required for the role or 'revoke' for access no longer needed.
Complete all assigned reviews before the campaign due date.
checklist.done: every assigned reviewer has attested approve or revoke on 100% of their entitlement reviews before the due date.

checklist.step: Revoke access for failed or unattested items
actions: At campaign close, pull the list of entitlements marked 'revoke' plus any left unattested past the due date.
Process the deprovisioning in the target application (remove role/group membership) and confirm removal.
Record the revocation date and confirming screenshot against each entitlement row in the campaign record.
checklist.done: every revoked or unattested entitlement is deprovisioned in the target system with a dated confirmation on file.

checklist.step: Rotate encryption keys per schedule
actions: Open the key management service console and confirm each in-scope key's rotation policy matches the documented standard (annual minimum, 90 days for high-sensitivity data).
Trigger manual rotation for any key past its scheduled rotation date.
Confirm dependent applications reconnect successfully after rotation before closing the task.
checklist.done: every encryption key is rotated per its documented schedule and dependent applications are confirmed working.

checklist.step: Monitor control exceptions via SIEM alerts
actions: In the SIEM console open the saved search/dashboard for MFA-bypass attempts, impossible-travel logins and unencrypted-protocol usage.
Triage each alert within the shift and confirm whether it represents a genuine control failure or a false positive.
Escalate confirmed control failures to the IT Security Manager and open a ticket.
checklist.done: SIEM alerts for MFA bypass, anomalous login and unencrypted transmission are triaged each shift with confirmed failures ticketed.

checklist.step: Remediate identified control gaps
actions: Consolidate control gaps from the MFA report, encryption verification and SIEM triage into remediation tickets.
Assign each ticket to the responsible system owner with a due date based on gap severity.
Track ticket status weekly until closure.
checklist.done: every identified control gap has an assigned, dated remediation ticket tracked to closure.

checklist.step: Validate remediation
actions: For each closed remediation ticket, re-check the specific control (MFA enrolment, encryption setting, or access revocation) in the source system.
Confirm the control now meets the documented baseline before signing off the ticket.
Reopen and reassign any ticket where the fix does not hold.
checklist.done: every closed remediation ticket is independently re-checked against the control baseline before final sign-off.

checklist.step: Report control operating effectiveness to the CISO
actions: Compile a monthly control dashboard: MFA coverage %, access-review campaign completion %, encryption exceptions and open remediation tickets.
Present the dashboard to the Chief Info Security Officer at the monthly security operations review.
Record any directive from the review and its target date.
checklist.done: a monthly control effectiveness dashboard is presented to the CISO with any directives recorded.

checklist.step: Log exceptions with disposition
actions: For every control gap that cannot be closed within the standard SLA, log a formal exception with root cause and a compensating control.
Route the exception to the IT Security Manager for approval and set an expiry/review date.
Track approved exceptions on the monthly dashboard until they are closed or renewed.
checklist.done: every unresolved control gap carries an approved, dated exception with a compensating control.

checklist.step: Retain evidence in the compliance repository
actions: Upload the MFA coverage reports, access-review campaign records, encryption verification logs and remediation tickets to the compliance evidence repository, organized by quarter.
Apply the 6-year retention label required under FCA Handbook SYSC 9.
Confirm the repository index is retrievable by system, control type and quarter.
checklist.done: the quarter's control evidence set is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by system and control type.

testing.step: Build the population of in-scope accounts and campaigns
actions: Export the full user and privileged account list from the IAM platform as of the test date, with MFA enrolment status.
Export the quarterly access-review campaign completion report.
Reconcile both extracts to the CMDB in-scope system list and resolve any mismatch before sampling.
testing.done: the account and campaign population reconciles to the CMDB in-scope system list.

testing.step: Verify MFA coverage on privileged and customer-data accounts
actions: Filter the account population to privileged accounts and accounts on customer-data-facing applications.
Confirm 100% of these accounts show an enrolled MFA factor in the extract.
List any account without MFA as an automatic exception with no judgement applied.
testing.done: every privileged and customer-data account is confirmed MFA-enrolled or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample for encryption and access-review testing
actions: Take 100% of privileged accounts flagged revoke-or-unattested in the quarterly campaign.
Take 25 additional standard accounts at random (seeded, reproducible) across in-scope systems.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all revoke/unattested privileged accounts.

testing.step: Re-perform the access-review outcome for the sample
actions: Open each sampled entitlement in the IAM platform and independently assess whether the access still matches the user's current role.
Compare the independent assessment to the recorded reviewer attestation.
Flag any mismatch, especially approvals for access outside the user's current role, as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled entitlement has an independent role-match assessment compared to the recorded attestation.

testing.step: Confirm revoked accounts were actually deprovisioned
actions: For each sampled account marked revoked, log in to the target application (or query its entitlement API) and confirm the access no longer exists.
Compare the deprovisioning timestamp to the campaign close date and flag any deprovisioning that happened late.
Capture the confirming screenshot or query output in the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled revoked account is confirmed deprovisioned in the target system, with timing checked.

testing.step: Test encryption configuration on the sample
actions: For each sampled in-scope system, independently query the database/storage encryption-at-rest setting and run a TLS scan against its endpoint.
Compare results to the documented control baseline for that data-sensitivity tier.
Flag any system below the required encryption standard as an exception.
testing.done: encryption-at-rest and TLS configuration is independently verified against the baseline for every sampled system.

testing.step: Recompute MFA and access-review SLA timing
actions: For the sampled campaign, recompute the 30-day completion window from the campaign launch date.
Compare the recomputed deadline to the actual campaign close date and flag any late completion.
Recompute the monthly MFA-report cadence and confirm no month in the period was skipped.
testing.done: campaign completion timing and MFA reporting cadence are recomputed and any lapse is flagged.

testing.step: Trace SIEM-flagged control failures to remediation tickets
actions: Pull the period's SIEM alerts for MFA bypass and unencrypted-protocol usage that were triaged as confirmed failures.
Trace each confirmed failure to its remediation ticket in the ITSM/security ticketing system and confirm closure evidence.
Flag any confirmed failure with no linked, closed ticket.
testing.done: every confirmed SIEM control failure traces to a closed remediation ticket, or is flagged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each test exception identified above.
Assign a root cause category (late deprovisioning, missed MFA enrolment, encryption misconfiguration) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into the next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the population and compare to the 100%-MFA and 98%-on-time-campaign thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence gathered.
Have the independent reviewer, who holds no IAM provisioning rights, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is reported and filed.

checklist.step: Plan and schedule the annual incident response tabletop exercise
actions: Select a scenario relevant to the current threat landscape (ransomware, third-party data breach, prolonged outage of an important business service).
Define exercise objectives: detection time, escalation path, notification-decision timing, and communications accuracy.
Schedule the exercise date and invite the Incident Response Lead, SOC Lead, General Counsel, Chief Risk Officer and Communications Specialist.
Publish the scenario brief and objectives to participants at least 5 business days ahead.
checklist.done: a scenario, objectives, date and participant list are confirmed and the brief is published in advance.

checklist.step: Run the tabletop exercise and capture the walkthrough
actions: Facilitate the scenario walkthrough, injecting decision points that require an escalation and notification call.
Record each participant's decision, the time taken, and whether it matched the documented plan step.
Capture gaps where the plan was unclear or a role was unstaffed.
checklist.done: the tabletop is run to completion with a timed decision log capturing every gap against the plan.

checklist.step: Score the exercise against its objectives and log findings
actions: Score each exercise objective (detection time, escalation, notification-decision timing, communications) as met, partially met or not met.
Log every not-met or partially-met objective as a finding with a proposed plan or staffing fix.
Circulate the scored report to the Chief Risk Officer within 5 business days of the exercise.
checklist.done: every exercise objective is scored and every gap is logged as a finding with a proposed fix.

checklist.step: Update the incident response plan from tabletop findings
actions: Revise the plan document to close each logged finding (clarify a step, add a contact, adjust a timeline).
Route the revised plan through the standard policy approval workflow for CISO and Board Risk Committee sign-off.
Republish the approved plan and notify all named responders of the change.
checklist.done: the plan is revised to address every finding, re-approved, and republished to responders.

checklist.step: Configure incident detection and severity classification
actions: In the SIEM/SOAR console confirm detection rules and correlation searches map to the plan's incident categories.
Verify the severity classification matrix (Sev 1-4) is loaded into the SOAR playbook with the correct escalation targets.
Test-fire a sample alert through the playbook and confirm it routes to the correct on-call responder.
checklist.done: detection rules and the severity matrix are verified live in the SOAR playbook with a successful routing test.

checklist.step: Detect and triage a live incident
actions: Open the triggering alert in the SIEM/SOAR console, confirm it is a genuine incident, and open an incident case.
Classify severity using the documented matrix and assign the Incident Response Lead as case owner.
Timestamp the detection time and start the incident timeline in the case record.
checklist.done: a triaged incident case exists with a severity classification, owner and a started timeline.

checklist.step: Assess whether the incident meets the FCA notification trigger
actions: Compare the incident's impact (data compromised, service outage duration, customer numbers affected) against the SUP 15.3 'serious regulatory impact' criteria.
Consult General Counsel where the trigger is ambiguous and record the joint decision on the case.
Log the notification-required decision, decider and time on the incident case.
checklist.done: a documented, timestamped notification-required decision exists on the incident case.

checklist.step: Draft and submit the FCA notification
actions: Draft the notification covering what happened, when detected, customer/market impact, and remediation steps taken so far.
Route the draft to the Chief Risk Officer for review before submission.
Submit via the firm's usual FCA supervisory contact channel or RegData as directed by the firm's supervisor, and record the submission timestamp.
checklist.done: the notification is drafted, reviewed and submitted with a recorded timestamp within the SUP 15.3 timeline.

checklist.step: Contain and remediate the incident
actions: Execute the containment playbook steps in SOAR (isolate host, revoke credentials, block indicator) and log each action with a timestamp.
Coordinate with system owners on remediation and verify the threat is eradicated before declaring containment complete.
Update the incident case status and timeline through to resolution.
checklist.done: containment and remediation actions are logged with timestamps and the case is updated through to resolution.

checklist.step: Notify affected customers where required
actions: Determine, with General Counsel, whether customer notification is required under UK GDPR Article 34 or the incident response plan's customer-impact criteria.
Draft the customer notification and route it for legal and Complaints Manager review before sending.
Log the notification content and send date against the incident case.
checklist.done: the customer notification decision is documented and any required notification is sent with a logged date.

checklist.step: Conduct the post-incident review
actions: Hold a post-incident review within 10 business days of resolution with all responders.
Document root cause, response timeline against the plan, and lessons learned.
Assign action owners and due dates for every lesson learned.
checklist.done: a post-incident review is held within 10 business days with root cause, timeline and owned action items documented.

checklist.step: Track post-incident and tabletop remediation actions to closure
actions: Open a ticket for each post-incident review and tabletop remediation action with owner and due date.
Follow up weekly on open items and escalate overdue actions to the Chief Info Security Officer.
Close each ticket only with evidence the action was completed.
checklist.done: every remediation action is ticketed, tracked and closed with evidence.

checklist.step: Report incident and tabletop outcomes to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Summarize the period's Severity 1/2 incidents, notification timeliness, and the tabletop scorecard in the Risk Committee pack.
Upload the pack to the board portal ahead of the meeting and present the summary.
Capture committee questions and directives against the record.
checklist.done: an incident and tabletop summary is uploaded to the board portal and presented, with directives captured.

checklist.step: Log exceptions with disposition
actions: Log any missed tabletop objective, late FCA notification, or overdue post-incident action as a formal exception with root cause.
Route each exception to the Chief Info Security Officer for a disposition and remediation date.
Track exceptions to closure on the monthly security dashboard.
checklist.done: every exception is logged with root cause, disposition and a tracked remediation date.

checklist.step: Retain incident and tabletop evidence in the compliance repository
actions: Upload the tabletop report, incident timelines, FCA notification correspondence and post-incident reviews to the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 6-year retention label required under FCA Handbook SYSC 9.
Confirm the folder is indexed and retrievable by incident id and exercise date.
checklist.done: the full evidence set is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by incident id and exercise date.

testing.step: Build the population of incidents and the tabletop exercise
actions: Export every Severity 1 and 2 incident case from the SIEM/SOAR platform for the period.
Add the annual tabletop exercise as a population item.
Reconcile the incident count to the ITSM/security ticketing system's incident category to confirm nothing was excluded.
testing.done: the incident and tabletop population reconciles between the SOAR platform and the ITSM ticketing system.

testing.step: Confirm the tabletop exercise met its scheduling and scope requirements
actions: Confirm the tabletop occurred within the annual cycle required by the plan.
Check the participant list against the required roles (Incident Response Lead, SOC Lead, General Counsel, Chief Risk Officer, Communications Specialist).
Flag any missing required participant or a cycle gap as an exception.
testing.done: tabletop timing and participation are checked against the plan requirement, with gaps flagged.

testing.step: Draw the sample of incidents for detailed testing
actions: Take 100% of Severity 1 incidents in the period.
Take 10 Severity 2 incidents at random (seeded, reproducible).
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers 100% of Severity 1 incidents.

testing.step: Re-perform the notification-trigger assessment for the sample
actions: For each sampled incident, independently assess against SUP 15.3 criteria whether FCA notification was required, using only the incident case evidence as it stood at the time.
Compare the independent assessment to the decision actually recorded on the case.
Flag any case where notification should have occurred but did not, as a Critical exception.
testing.done: each sampled incident has an independent notification-trigger assessment compared to the recorded decision.

testing.step: Trace notified incidents to the submitted FCA correspondence
actions: For each sampled incident where notification was required, locate the actual submission (email, RegData confirmation, or supervisory call note).
Confirm the submission content matches the incident facts as known at submission time and covers impact and remediation status.
Capture the submission evidence into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled notification-required incident traces to actual, content-matching FCA correspondence.

testing.step: Recompute the notification timeline against the SUP 15.3 deadline
actions: For each sampled notified incident, recompute the time elapsed between detection timestamp and notification submission timestamp.
Compare the elapsed time to the plan's internal target and the SUP 15.3 'without undue delay' standard.
Flag any notification that took longer than the plan's internal target with no documented justification.
testing.done: notification timing is recomputed for every sampled incident, with unjustified delays flagged.

testing.step: Verify post-incident review completion and action closure
actions: Confirm a post-incident review record exists for each sampled Severity 1/2 incident within 10 business days of resolution.
Trace each review's action items to closed tickets with completion evidence.
Flag any review missing, late, or with an open action past its due date.
testing.done: post-incident review existence, timing and action closure are verified for every sampled incident.

testing.step: Confirm tabletop findings were remediated in the plan
actions: Compare the tabletop scored report's not-met/partially-met objectives to the revised plan document.
Confirm the plan revision date is after the tabletop and that the specific gap was addressed in the text.
Flag any tabletop finding with no corresponding plan revision.
testing.done: every tabletop finding is traced to a dated plan revision, or flagged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each test exception identified above.
Assign a root cause category (late notification, missed trigger, unclosed action) and an owner.
Set a remediation date; any missed FCA notification also triggers a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date, and missed notifications trigger a self-report assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare to the zero-tolerance threshold for missed/late FCA notifications.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence gathered.
Have the independent reviewer, who did not participate in incident response or tabletop design, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any open breaches to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is reported to the Board Risk Committee and filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual certification of compliance with the firm's information security controls, filed in support of the SM&CR Certification Regime

Citation verified against current regula.value: FCA Handbook SYSC 27.9 (Certification Regime — annual certification of Certified Persons) and SYSC 4.3 (management responsibility), re-read at certification date (rep: United Kingdom)

In-scope processes.value: Year-end assessment of every Certified Person in a Certification Function role touching information security or customer data, and the resulting fit-and-proper annual certification filing

In-scope systems.value: Certification workflow, evidence collection and sign-off tracked in the GRC platform; certificates issued and filed via HRIS and the Internal Regulatory System

Compliance procedure documented.value: Annual Certification Regime Procedure — competence assessment, conduct rule breach check, fitness-and-propriety declaration, certificate issuance

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Info Security Officer and Head of Compliance; reviewed annually ahead of the certification window

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual certification must be completed and each certificate issued or refused within 12 months of the prior certification, per SYSC 27.9

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC platform reminders at T-60/T-30/T-10 days to each Certified Person's certification anniversary date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Competence assessments, conduct rule breach checks, fitness declarations and issued certificates retained 6 years per FCA Handbook SYSC 9

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any certification completed late, or any refusal to certify, is logged as an exception with disposition and HR/Compliance follow-up

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Every late certification and every refusal-to-certify case is signed off with its final disposition

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All individuals holding a Certification Function as of the certification window, per the HRIS Certification Regime role list

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of Certified Persons must have a completed certification decision (certified or refused) before their anniversary date to pass

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the test runs once per certification cycle over the full Certified Person population

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have performed any certification assessment being tested

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual certification test workpaper (population extract, sample, assessment re-performance, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Certification population list, completed certificates and any refusal records, presentable within 5 business days of an FCA request

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance owns the response; General Counsel clears any submission referencing a refused certification

checklist.step: Pull the Certification Function population
actions: In the HRIS, filter active employees by Certification Function tag for roles with system access to information security controls or customer data.
Cross-check the list against the CISO's own team roster and any contractor holding a Certification Function.
Load the confirmed population into the GRC platform's certification workflow module.
checklist.done: the confirmed Certification Function population is loaded into the GRC platform certification workflow.

checklist.step: Open a certification case for each Certified Person
actions: In the GRC platform open Certification ▸ New Case for each individual, pre-populated from HRIS with role, tenure and prior certification date.
Set the case due date to 12 months minus 30 days from the individual's last certification date.
Assign the case to the individual's line manager for the competence and conduct assessment.
checklist.done: every Certified Person has an open, due-dated certification case assigned to their line manager.

checklist.step: Assess competence against the role profile
actions: Review the individual's completed mandatory training, performance review outcomes and any skills gaps against the role profile for the Certification Function.
Document the competence conclusion (competent / development needed / not competent) on the certification case.
Where development needed, attach the training plan and target completion date.
checklist.done: a documented competence conclusion, with a training plan where applicable, exists on every case.

checklist.step: Check for conduct rule breaches in the period
actions: Query the disciplinary and conduct-breach register for any record against the individual since the last certification.
Where a breach is recorded, retrieve the investigation outcome and any sanction applied.
Attach the breach record and outcome, or confirm 'no breach found', to the certification case.
checklist.done: every certification case shows either a confirmed breach outcome or a documented 'no breach found' check.

checklist.step: Complete the fitness-and-propriety declaration
actions: Run the required background checks (criminal record, credit check, regulatory reference) per the firm's onboarding-refresh schedule.
Complete the fitness-and-propriety declaration form covering honesty, integrity, reputation, competence and financial soundness.
Attach the check results and declaration to the certification case.
checklist.done: background checks are completed and a fitness-and-propriety declaration is attached to the case.

checklist.step: Take the certification decision
actions: Review the competence conclusion, conduct check and fitness declaration together against the certification standard.
Decide to certify or refuse to certify, and record the reasoning on the case.
Where refusing, notify HR Business Partner and Compliance Manager immediately for the statutory next-steps process.
checklist.done: a reasoned certify/refuse decision is recorded on every case.

checklist.step: Issue the certificate
actions: For certified individuals, generate the certificate from the GRC platform template with the certification period and function.
Deliver the certificate to the individual and file the acknowledgement of receipt.
Update the individual's HRIS record with the new certification expiry date.
checklist.done: a certificate is issued, acknowledged and the HRIS expiry date is updated for every certified individual.

checklist.step: Process refusal-to-certify cases
actions: For any refused individual, initiate the SM&CR-required process: restrict system access to information-security functions and notify the Chief Info Security Officer.
Coordinate with HR Business Partner on the individual's role change, remediation plan, or termination per policy.
Assess whether the refusal itself is a notifiable event to the FCA and consult General Counsel.
checklist.done: every refusal triggers access restriction, an HR action plan, and an FCA-notifiability assessment.

checklist.step: Track certification cases to closure against the deadline
actions: Run a weekly report of open certification cases filtered by due date within 30 days.
Follow up with line managers on overdue assessments and log the reason for delay.
Escalate cases more than 10 days past due to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: a weekly report tracks open cases and every case more than 10 days overdue is escalated.

checklist.step: Consolidate the annual certification summary
actions: Compile the count of certified, refused, and still-open cases across the population.
Note any case closed after its anniversary date and the reason.
Prepare the summary for the Head of Compliance's sign-off.
checklist.done: a consolidated summary of certification outcomes across the full population is prepared.

checklist.step: Obtain Head of Compliance sign-off on the annual certification
actions: Review the consolidated summary and the underlying case files for completeness.
Sign off the annual certification cycle as complete, noting any residual open case and its remediation plan.
File the signed summary with the annual SM&CR governance pack.
checklist.done: the Head of Compliance signs off the cycle summary, with any residual open case and its remediation plan noted.

checklist.step: Report certification outcomes to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Upload the certification summary to the board portal ahead of the scheduled governance meeting.
Present the completion rate, any refusals and their status, and any overdue cases.
Capture committee questions and directives against the record.
checklist.done: the certification summary is uploaded and presented to the Board Risk Committee, with directives captured.

checklist.step: Log exceptions with disposition
actions: Log every case completed after its anniversary date as a formal exception with root cause.
Route the exception to the Head of Compliance for disposition.
Record the disposition and any process fix to prevent recurrence.
checklist.done: every late certification case has a logged exception with root cause and disposition.

checklist.step: Retain certification evidence for the retention period
actions: Move each closed certification case (competence assessment, conduct check, fitness declaration, decision, certificate) into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 6-year retention label required under FCA Handbook SYSC 9.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by individual and certification year.
checklist.done: every closed case is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by individual and certification year.

testing.step: Build the population of Certified Persons
actions: Extract the Certification Function-tagged population from the HRIS as of the certification window.
Reconcile the extract to the GRC platform's certification case list to confirm every individual has an open or closed case.
Resolve any individual missing a case with the Security GRC Analyst before sampling.
testing.done: the Certified Person population reconciles between HRIS and the GRC platform certification workflow.

testing.step: Confirm 100% case completion before each anniversary date
actions: For every individual in the population, compare the certification case close date to their certification anniversary date.
List any case open past its anniversary date as an automatic exception.
Note any individual with no case opened at all as a Critical exception.
testing.done: every population member's case timing is checked against their anniversary date, with lapses listed.

testing.step: Draw the sample of certification cases
actions: Take 100% of refusal-to-certify cases.
Take 20 certified cases at random (seeded, reproducible).
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers 100% of refusal cases.

testing.step: Re-perform the conduct rule breach check on the sample
actions: Independently query the disciplinary and conduct-breach register for each sampled individual over the certification period.
Compare the independent result to what is documented on the certification case.
Flag any case where a breach existed but was not reflected in the certification decision.
testing.done: each sampled case's conduct check is independently re-performed and compared to the recorded result.

testing.step: Verify the fitness-and-propriety evidence on the sample
actions: Confirm the required background checks (criminal record, credit, regulatory reference) are present and dated within the certification window for each sampled case.
Confirm the declaration form is signed by the individual and countersigned by the line manager.
Flag any missing or stale (prior-cycle) evidence.
testing.done: fitness-and-propriety evidence completeness and currency are verified for every sampled case.

testing.step: Re-perform the competence assessment for the sample
actions: Review the training records and performance outcomes behind each sampled competence conclusion.
Independently form a competence view and compare it to the recorded conclusion.
Flag any conclusion that appears unsupported by the underlying evidence.
testing.done: each sampled competence conclusion is independently checked against its supporting evidence.

testing.step: Trace certificates issued to HRIS expiry-date updates
actions: For each sampled certified case, confirm a certificate document exists with the correct certification period.
Confirm the HRIS record shows the matching updated expiry date.
Flag any certificate not reflected in HRIS.
testing.done: certificate issuance is traced to a matching HRIS expiry-date update for every sampled case.

testing.step: Verify refusal-case follow-through
actions: For each refusal case in the sample, confirm access restriction to information-security functions was applied and dated.
Confirm the FCA-notifiability assessment was completed and, where notification was required, trace it to the actual submission.
Flag any refusal case missing the access restriction or the notifiability assessment.
testing.done: every sampled refusal case shows access restriction and a completed notifiability assessment, or is flagged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a case-level exception for each finding above, describing the gap.
Assign a root cause category (late assessment, missing evidence, unlinked refusal action) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry unresolved items into next cycle's mandatory retest population.
testing.done: every exception has a logged root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the population and compare to the 100%-completion threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence gathered.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed none of the sampled assessments, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is reported and filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns oversight of critical/important third-party service provider security across the outsourcing portfolio

Citation verified against current regula.value: FCA Handbook SYSC 8 (outsourcing) and PRA Rulebook / SS2/21 (Outsourcing and third party risk management), re-read at each vendor risk assessment (rep: United Kingdom)

In-scope processes.value: Due diligence, contracting, ongoing monitoring and exit planning for every critical or important outsourced function, per the outsourcing register

In-scope systems.value: Vendor risk assessments, security questionnaires and monitoring results tracked in the GRC platform; contracts held in the contract lifecycle management repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Third-Party Outsourcing Oversight Procedure — criticality assessment, pre-contract due diligence, security questionnaire, contract clause standard, ongoing monitoring cadence, exit plan requirement

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Info Security Officer and Third-Party Risk Manager; reviewed annually

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Pre-contract due diligence completed before any critical/important function goes live; annual reassessment for every critical vendor; exit plan reviewed every 2 years

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC platform reminders at T-60/T-30 days to each vendor's annual reassessment date and each contract's renewal/exit-plan review date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Due diligence packs, security questionnaires, monitoring results, contracts and exit plans retained 6 years after contract termination per FCA Handbook SYSC 9

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any vendor operating past its due diligence or reassessment date, or with an unresolved critical security finding, is logged as an exception

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Every closed vendor security finding and every overdue reassessment is signed off with remediation evidence

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All vendors classified critical or important on the outsourcing register as of the test date

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of critical/important vendors must have a current (within 12 months) security reassessment and an executed contract with the standard security clauses to pass

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per-vendor/annual; the test runs annually over the full critical/important vendor population

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have performed any sampled vendor assessment

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual third-party oversight test workpaper (vendor population, sample, re-performed due diligence checks, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Outsourcing register extract, vendor risk assessments and contracts, presentable within 5 business days of a supervisory request

Regulator response path.value: Third-Party Risk Manager owns the response; Procurement Manager and General Counsel support contract-specific queries

checklist.step: Maintain the outsourcing register and criticality classification
actions: In the GRC platform open the Vendor/Outsourcing module and review each active vendor's function description.
Apply the criticality test (impact of failure on important business services, data sensitivity, substitutability) and classify as Critical, Important or Standard.
Add any newly onboarded vendor to the register within 5 business days of contract signature.
Confirm the register reconciles to the Coupa/Ariba active supplier list.
checklist.done: the outsourcing register is current, every vendor is classified, and it reconciles to the active supplier list.

checklist.step: Run pre-contract due diligence for a new critical/important vendor
actions: Issue the standard security questionnaire (SOC 2 report request, penetration test summary, data handling and sub-outsourcing disclosure) to the prospective vendor.
Review the vendor's SOC 2/ISO 27001 certificate and any exceptions noted in the auditor's opinion.
Score the vendor's residual risk and document the go/no-go recommendation.
checklist.done: a completed security questionnaire, certificate review and a documented risk score exist before contract signature.

checklist.step: Negotiate the required outsourcing contract clauses
actions: In Coupa/Ariba open the contract request and attach the standard SYSC 8 clause pack (audit rights, sub-outsourcing notification, data location, breach notification timeline, termination/exit assistance).
Route the draft to General Counsel for review of any vendor-proposed deviation.
Confirm the final signed contract includes every required clause before activation.
checklist.done: the executed contract includes every required SYSC 8 clause, confirmed before activation.

checklist.step: File the contract and due diligence pack in the contract repository
actions: Upload the executed contract, due diligence pack and risk score to the contract lifecycle management repository, linked to the vendor's outsourcing register entry.
Tag the record with the criticality classification and the annual reassessment due date.
Confirm the repository record is retrievable from the outsourcing register.
checklist.done: the contract and due diligence pack are filed, tagged and linked to the register entry.

checklist.step: Set the ongoing monitoring cadence
actions: Configure the GRC platform to trigger an annual reassessment task for every Critical/Important vendor and a lighter-touch biennial review for Standard vendors.
Set continuous monitoring alerts (breach notification feeds, financial health score) for Critical vendors where the tool supports it.
Confirm the monitoring configuration against the register at least quarterly.
checklist.done: annual/biennial reassessment tasks and continuous monitoring alerts are configured for every vendor tier.

checklist.step: Perform the annual vendor security reassessment
actions: Request the vendor's current SOC 2/ISO 27001 report and any material change disclosure (ownership, sub-outsourcing, breach history) since the last assessment.
Compare the current report to the prior year and flag any new exception or control gap.
Update the vendor's risk score and record the reassessment date on the register.
checklist.done: an updated risk score and reassessment date are recorded for every Critical/Important vendor within its annual cycle.

checklist.step: Investigate any vendor security incident or breach notification
actions: On receiving a vendor breach notification, open an incident case and assess the impact to the firm's data or important business services.
Coordinate with the Chief Info Security Officer on whether the firm's own incident response and FCA notification process is triggered.
Document the vendor's remediation commitment and set a follow-up review date.
checklist.done: every vendor breach notification is assessed for firm impact, with a documented remediation follow-up date.

checklist.step: Track vendor remediation of open security findings
actions: Log each open vendor security finding (from SOC 2 exceptions or incidents) in the GRC platform with a target remediation date.
Follow up with the vendor relationship owner at each monitoring cadence until the finding is confirmed closed.
Escalate a finding open beyond two monitoring cycles to the Chief Info Security Officer.
checklist.done: every open vendor finding is tracked with a remediation date and escalated if it persists past two cycles.

checklist.step: Review and refresh the exit plan for each critical vendor
actions: Review the documented exit/transition plan for feasibility: alternative provider, data extraction method, and estimated transition timeline.
Confirm the plan reflects the vendor's current service scope and any sub-outsourcing arrangement.
Re-approve or update the plan at least every 2 years, or immediately after a material service change.
checklist.done: every critical vendor's exit plan is current, feasible and re-approved within the 2-year cycle.

checklist.step: Escalate any vendor operating without current due diligence
actions: Identify any Critical/Important vendor whose reassessment or contract clause coverage has lapsed.
Raise the gap to the Third-Party Risk Manager and the vendor relationship owner for immediate remediation.
Where the gap cannot close within 30 days, escalate to the Board Risk Committee with a risk-acceptance or termination recommendation.
checklist.done: every lapsed vendor is escalated and, if unresolved within 30 days, brought to the Board Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Consolidate the annual outsourcing oversight report
actions: Compile the vendor population, reassessment completion rate, open findings and exit-plan status into the annual report.
Circulate the draft to the Chief Info Security Officer and Chief Risk Officer for review.
Finalize the report ahead of the Board Risk Committee cycle.
checklist.done: a consolidated annual outsourcing oversight report is finalized and reviewed.

checklist.step: Present the outsourcing oversight report to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Upload the finalized report to the board portal ahead of the scheduled meeting.
Present the vendor risk landscape, reassessment coverage and any unresolved critical findings.
Capture committee directives against the record.
checklist.done: the report is uploaded, presented, and committee directives are captured.

checklist.step: Log exceptions with disposition
actions: Log every lapsed reassessment, missing clause, or unremediated finding as a formal exception with root cause.
Route each exception to the Chief Info Security Officer for disposition and a remediation date.
Track approved exceptions until closed.
checklist.done: every gap is logged as an exception with root cause, disposition and a tracked remediation date.

checklist.step: Retain vendor oversight evidence for the retention period
actions: Upload due diligence packs, reassessments, incident records, exit plans and the annual report to the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 6-year-post-termination retention label per FCA Handbook SYSC 9.
Confirm the repository index is retrievable by vendor and criticality tier.
checklist.done: the full vendor oversight evidence set is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by vendor and tier.

testing.step: Build the population of critical/important vendors
actions: Export the full outsourcing register filtered to Critical and Important classification.
Reconcile the register to the Coupa/Ariba active supplier list to confirm no critical vendor is missing from the register.
Resolve any mismatch with the Third-Party Risk Manager before sampling.
testing.done: the vendor population reconciles between the outsourcing register and the active supplier list.

testing.step: Verify classification consistency across the population
actions: Independently apply the criticality test to a cross-section of vendors using the function description on file.
Compare the independent classification to the recorded classification.
Flag any vendor that appears under-classified relative to its actual function.
testing.done: classification consistency is checked and any apparent under-classification is flagged.

testing.step: Draw the sample of vendors
actions: Take 100% of Critical vendors.
Take 15 Important vendors at random (seeded, reproducible).
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers 100% of Critical vendors.

testing.step: Re-perform the due diligence check on the sample
actions: For each sampled vendor, independently review the current SOC 2/ISO 27001 report and confirm no material exception was missed in the recorded reassessment.
Compare the independent review to the recorded risk score.
Flag any material exception omitted from the recorded assessment.
testing.done: each sampled vendor's due diligence evidence is independently reviewed and compared to the recorded score.

testing.step: Verify contract clause coverage on the sample
actions: Open each sampled vendor's executed contract in the repository and check for the required SYSC 8 clause set (audit rights, sub-outsourcing notification, breach notification timeline, exit assistance).
Flag any missing or weakened clause compared to the standard clause pack.
Note the contract execution date relative to the service go-live date.
testing.done: clause coverage is verified for every sampled contract, with gaps and timing issues flagged.

testing.step: Recompute reassessment timing against the annual cycle
actions: For each sampled vendor, recompute the 12-month reassessment window from the prior assessment date.
Compare the recomputed window to the actual reassessment completion date.
Flag any vendor reassessed late or not at all in the period.

File the confirmation with the filing record.
checklist.done: the SUP 16 return is submitted through RegData with a downloaded, filed acceptance confirmation.

checklist.step: Track filings against the deadline calendar
actions: Update the close calendar with each filing's actual submission date and status.
Flag any filing at risk of missing its deadline at T-5 days and escalate to the Chief Financial Officer.
Confirm every entity's filing is marked submitted before the deadline passes.
checklist.done: the close calendar reflects actual submission status for every entity, with at-risk filings escalated before deadline.

checklist.step: Respond to regulator filing queries or edit rejections
actions: Monitor the NAIC/FCA portal for any rejected edit check or examiner query on the submitted filing.
Research and prepare the response or corrected schedule within the regulator's stated response window.
Resubmit the corrected filing and log the correction with its reason.
checklist.done: every rejected edit or examiner query is answered within the response window, with any correction logged.

checklist.step: Assess and process any post-filing restatement
actions: Where a material error is identified after filing, assess the restatement requirement against NAIC/FCA guidance.
Prepare and file the amended statement/return, with General Counsel review of any required regulator notification.
Document the root cause and the process fix to prevent recurrence.
checklist.done: any material post-filing error is assessed, restated where required, notified, and root-caused.

checklist.step: Log exceptions with disposition
actions: Log any missed deadline, rejected edit unresolved past its window, or restatement as a formal exception with root cause.
Route each exception to the Chief Financial Officer for disposition.
Track exceptions to closure and reflect resolution in the close calendar.
checklist.done: every filing exception is logged with root cause, disposition and tracked closure.

checklist.step: Retain filing evidence for the retention period
actions: Upload each filed statement/return, supporting trial balance, actuarial sign-off and submission confirmation to the financial reporting repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label required under FCA Handbook SYSC 9 and applicable NAIC record-retention requirements.
Confirm the repository index is retrievable by entity, period and filing type.
checklist.done: the full filing evidence set is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by entity, period and type.

testing.step: Build the population of statutory filings for the period
actions: Extract every quarterly and annual statutory filing due in the period from the close calendar, by entity and filing type.
Reconcile the extract to the actual submissions recorded in the Statutory Reporting (NAIC) system and the Internal Regulatory System.
Resolve any calendar-to-submission mismatch before sampling.
testing.done: the filing population reconciles between the close calendar and the actual filing systems.

testing.step: Confirm on-time submission for every filing in the population
actions: Compare each filing's submission confirmation timestamp to its statutory due date.
List any filing submitted after its due date as an automatic exception.
Confirm every late filing has a logged root cause and regulator communication.
testing.done: every filing's timeliness is checked against its due date, with late filings and their disposition confirmed.

testing.step: Draw the sample of filings for detailed testing
actions: Take 100% of annual statutory filings and any filing that was late or restated.
Take 5 quarterly filings at random (seeded, reproducible) per entity.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers 100% of annual and late/restated filings.

testing.step: Recompute statutory adjustments and reconcile to the trial balance
actions: For each sampled NAIC blank, independently trace the SAP-to-STAT adjustments back to the locked trial balance and supporting schedules.
Recompute key totals (admitted assets, surplus, net income) and compare to the filed figures.
Flag any variance beyond the materiality threshold.
testing.done: statutory adjustments and key totals are independently recomputed and compared to the filed figures for every sampled blank.

testing.step: Recompute the UK SUP 16 return figures
actions: For each sampled SUP 16 return, independently re-map the trial balance to the return template.
Compare the independently mapped figures to the filed return.
Flag any mapping discrepancy.
testing.done: SUP 16 return figures are independently re-mapped and compared to the filed return for every sampled item.

testing.step: Verify reserve figures against the actuarial workpaper
actions: For each sampled filing, compare the filed reserve figures to the actuarial workpaper and the signed actuarial opinion.
Confirm the actuarial sign-off date precedes the filing submission date.
Flag any mismatch or missing/late sign-off.
testing.done: reserve figures and actuarial sign-off timing are verified against the workpaper for every sampled filing.

testing.step: Confirm CFO certification exists for every sampled filing
actions: Confirm the officer certification/attestation page is signed and dated by the Chief Financial Officer for each sampled filing.
Confirm the certification date precedes the actual submission date.
Flag any filing submitted without a valid, pre-dated certification.
testing.done: CFO certification existence and timing are verified for every sampled filing.

testing.step: Trace edit-check rejections and examiner queries to resolution
actions: For each sampled filing, check the regulator portal history for any rejected edit or examiner query.
Trace each query/rejection to a documented response and, where applicable, a resubmission within the regulator's response window.
Flag any unresolved query or a response that missed its window.
testing.done: edit-check rejections and examiner queries are traced to timely resolution for every sampled filing.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each test exception identified above.
Assign a root cause category (late filing, calculation error, missing certification) and an owner.
Set a remediation date; any material misstatement also triggers a formal restatement assessment.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date, and material misstatements trigger a restatement assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the population and compare to the zero-tolerance threshold for missed deadlines.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence gathered.
Have an independent reviewer who prepared or reviewed none of the sampled filings sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is reported to the Audit Committee and filed.
